summary: On 10 October 2017 a disk array failure on GoCardless's Postgres primary should have caused an automatic promotion of the synchronous replica. Pacemaker did not promote it, and the API and dashboard were down for about 1 hour 50 minutes until engineers promoted it by hand.

overview.background: GoCardless ran a Postgres cluster managed by Pacemaker, with a synchronous replica to take over on failure.
overview.impact: All requests failed for about 1 hour 50 minutes.
overview.severity: A full outage of the API and dashboard.

archNote: Components and relationships come from the cited source where it describes them. Layout and labels are ours.

diagrams.title: A cluster rule prevents promotion
diagrams.caption: Per GoCardless, three conditions together stopped Pacemaker promoting the replica: a non-zero resource stickiness, a Backup VIP colocated against the primary running on the replica, and near-simultaneous Postgres crashes.

nodes.label: Pacemaker refuses to promote the replica
Engineers promote the replica by hand

diagrams.title: Rule reversed and new cluster (as described by GoCardless)
diagrams.caption: GoCardless reversed the colocation rule so the Backup VIP prefers a replica, tested the failure, and moved to a new cluster with a PgBouncer switchover.

nodes.label: New Postgres cluster via PgBouncer switchover

afterChanges: Engineers can promote by hand quickly.
afterNote: The after picture shows the corrective ideas in the source and general good practice. It is conceptual unless the source says otherwise.
timelineNote: Times are as published by the source. Entries without a clock time are given in order only.

timeline.e: Evidence of a disk array failure on the primary.
The broken primary is powered off.
Clearing Pacemaker error counts has no effect; the cluster will not promote the replica.
Engineers manually promote the replica and point applications at its address.
The promoted primary is working and configuration changes roll out.
Monitoring confirms the API and dashboard are back.

rootCause.trigger: The primary's RAID controller lost three disks at once.
rootCause.underlying: A Pacemaker rule configuration stopped the promotion of the synchronous replica.
contributing: Backup VIP colocated against the primary on the replica
Manual recovery skills had eroded with automation

evidence.label: Impact
evidence.body: Any requests made during that time failed, and returned an error.
evidence.note: From the incident review summary as read.

evidence.label: The lesson
evidence.body: Seemingly simple Pacemaker configuration can lead to extremely unusual behaviour.

diagnose.step: Check cluster status and error counts.

verify.step: Check API and dashboard requests succeed.

fix.safety: Promoting a replica while the old primary may still be running risks split brain. Power off the old primary first.

troubleshoot.scenario: The Postgres primary has failed and the cluster will not promote the replica. Requests fail.
troubleshoot.question: What do you do?
hints: How do you avoid split brain?
troubleshoot.answer: Power off the broken primary, promote the replica by hand, repoint apps, then reproduce and fix the cluster rules.

remediation.answer: Kill primary and replica together in staging.

design.prompt: Design a failover that cannot be blocked by one rule.
design.answer: Simple rules, tested failure modes, fencing, manual runbooks and monitoring of promotion events.

checks.q: Was the invalid WAL file the cause?
options: No, it was a red herring

checks.q: What is the fix to the colocation rule?
options: Reverse it so the VIP prefers a replica
A new Postgres cluster using PgBouncer switchover
